turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his actions were not a threat, but a statement of fact, and that he had been documenting the instances of oppression against his tenantry, and would not hesitate to take further action if necessary.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip should not be under any illusion that he would tolerate such oppressive behavior any longer.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if his actions were indeed driven by a desire to protect his tenantry, or if there was another motive at play, her voice a calm and measured inquiry.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip if he had any knowledge of the circumstances leading to Nikhil's accusations, her eyes fixed intently on her husband's face.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled and told Nikhil that it was quite amusing to see him playing the role of a champion of the oppressed, given his own reputation for being as ruthless as a tiger

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip sneered at Nikhil, asking if he had finally gone mad, thinking he could intimidate him with his empty threats.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip if the tension between him and Nikhil had anything to do with their past dealings, her tone neutral and inquiring.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil to explain the specific incidents that had led to his accusations, her voice steady and inquiring.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip scoffed at Nikhil, remarking that his warnings sounded like the ravings of a madman, and asked if he had any proof to back up his claims

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was wasting his breath with such feeble attempts at intimidation, and that he had more pressing matters to attend to, like tending to his poetry

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala turned to Sandip and asked, with a hint of concern, what he thought the consequences would be if the local Mussulmans were indeed planning an attack on their estate.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip's poetry was a frivolous indulgence and that the threat of an attack should not be taken lightly

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was trying to deflect attention from his own family's debts, which had been a topic of whispered conversation in the village for weeks.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he thought the zamindar's estate was adequately prepared to defend itself against an attack, her voice neutral and inquiring.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip snorted in derision, telling Nikhil that he was more worried about the state of his own poetry than the state of the zamindar's defenses.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil stated that the zamindar's estate was not just a matter of personal concern, but also a responsibility to the entire community.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that any complacency on his part would be a dereliction of duty, and would put the entire community at risk.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: He cautioned Sandip to take immediate action to strengthen the estate's defenses, before it was too late.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed, a low, mocking sound, and said that Nikhil was so worked up over nothing, the Mussulmans would probably be the ones to thank him for his poetic efforts at defense.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled and asked Nikhil if he had considered the possibility that the Mussulmans were merely trying to distract him from the more pressing issue of Nikhil's own questionable land dealings.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
